title: Implement private MinIO candidate staging and cleanup

gates.name: Python typecheck
gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Candidate staging tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/inventory/test_candidate_staging.py

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-011 RED: inventory cannot stage one request-scoped candidate under a unique opaque private key and idempotently delete only that owned object; GREEN: disposable put/read/delete/repeat observations affect exactly the owned candidate and no other object; decisive comparison: before/after object inventory contains only the expected task-owned change and returns to the known empty scoped state; artifact: isolated MinIO probe output and object inventory.

FT-001-AC-011 RED_NOT_APPLICABLE: before a candidate path exists, absence of browser/log exposure cannot reveal a leak, and deliberately exposing real commercial bytes or credentials would violate the authorized proof boundary; alternative proof: use synthetic byte, opaque-key and dummy-credential markers after implementation, preserve the Foundation private-MinIO topology, and assert that browser-facing output, URLs and application logs contain none of those markers; decisive comparison: all marker scans are empty and only the HTTPS edge is browser-reachable; artifact: redacted security/topology output plus Foundation evidence references.
purpose: Provide the private, request-owned object boundary used before JPEG validation and PostgreSQL arbitration.
success_outcome: Inventory can stage one candidate under a unique opaque private MinIO key and idempotently clean only that request-owned object without exposing storage identity or credentials.
anti_goals: Do not persist Photos, arbitrate duplicates, open database transactions or implement orphan cleanup lifecycle.
Do not expose presigned/direct-MinIO browser access, object keys, storage credentials, versioning or external snapshots.

forbidden_scope: PostgreSQL Photo/pending admission and duplicate decisions
Public media delivery or browser storage access
Production MinIO data, credentials or bucket changes
stop_conditions: The candidate cannot remain private without changing the accepted deployment boundary.
Cleanup would need to discover or delete objects not owned by the current request.
A distributed transaction, object versioning or orphan lifecycle becomes necessary.

constraints: inventory owns candidate semantics; infrastructure supplies only the S3 adapter.
Every candidate key is unique, opaque and scoped to one request in the configured private bucket.
Isolated probes use disposable task-owned objects and retain safe-rerun cleanup evidence.
invariants: The browser receives no object key, storage credential or direct MinIO access.
Handled cleanup affects only the request-owned candidate and is idempotent.
This task creates no database admission or durable orphan lifecycle.
verification_targets: Isolated MinIO write/read/delete/repeat and topology/redaction proof records known initial state, owned cleanup and zero forbidden exposure.
